newsitem.title: UK: Cruise Holdings held talks over Cunard acquisition.
newsitem.headline: Cruise Holdings held talks over Cunard acquisition.

text.p: Cruise Holdings Ltd told Reuters on Monday it held talks with Norway's Kvaerner ASA on the acquisition of its Cunard cruise line, but it has rejected any deal a present due to a high asking price.
"We have had some discussions with Kvaerner about Cunard," Cruise Holdings chairman and chief executive officer Larry Magnan told Reuters.
"We would be very interested in Cunard. But at this point in time they are asking too much money for it, quite frankly."
Kvaerner acquired Cunard when it bought UK conglomerate Trafalgar House from Hongkong Land early last year.
But the Norwegian engineering and shipbuilding group has said it intends to sell non-core assets, including shipping activities.
Cunard is one of the world's most prestigious cruise brands, although its image has been tarnished in recent years by a series of blunders. It owns the Queen Elizabeth II.
"They (Kvaerner) have made it perfectly clear to us and everyone else, that the company (Cunard) is on the market and they are entertaining offers," Magnan said.
Cruise Holdings currently operates a fleet of five 'classic' cruise liners in the mass market. It intends to expand and further consolidate this niche market, Magnan said.
Earlier today, the firm said it would seek an initial public offering in Oslo in the next six months and has signed an letter of intent to buy the Rotterdam from Carnival Corp.

"We think that there are worldwide no more than 10-12 further ships that would fit into our market niche," said Magnan. "That is ships of the quality and that would not require massive expenditures to bring them up to snuff -- either from a ship safety, or from an interior decor standpoint.
"The Cunard ships are part of the 10-12 ships around the world that we would be interested in.
"One of the reasons we're going to public was to raise some money for a war chest so we can go out an write a cheque for some these ships," he added.
